status: FROZEN v3 BEFORE v3 RUNS (v1/v2 outputs preserved). v3 = the v2 specification re-run with solver v3 (tail-clip correction: v1/v2 lifted the overfall tail floor to pool_floor after the first bed update, leaving hydraulics unconverged, storage up to 3% of Q; effect on coarse partition <=2e-4 in f). Predictions and criteria unchanged from v2. Development basis: v1 evaluation results are now DEVELOPMENT information for this addendum; the bracket days, counterfactual and finest-grid check are new.
model_class: 2-D depth-averaged free-surface hydrodynamics (hydrostatic shallow water) with coupled thermal incision; idealised obstacles (solid raised bed / Ergun drag); not natural boulder behaviour.

solver.code_change_v2: ADDITIVE: region heat/melt accounting, bed snapshots, optional incision='uniform' counterfactual. Default physics unchanged (verified: v2 coarse strip f_toe series bit-identical to v1 for the first 6 updates; full 21-d identity is checked in analysis and v1 results kept).

geometry_and_physics: identical to v1 spec (frozen/production_spec.json) except where 'extra' says otherwise

counterfactual.name: differential incision disabled
counterfactual.definition: the same total melt volume of each bed update is spread uniformly over ALL ice cells (reach + entrance ramps) so routes/shielded and open cells lower equally; heat extraction, latent ledger and hydraulics are unchanged. Prediction: no stage-lowering relative to the strip crest => no contact loss and full recovery if removal.

identical_footprint_comparison.regions: toe_fp = deposit footprint cells of the toe reach (0.5 m2 for strip and corridor), toe_open = other toe-reach cells (corridor: 0.5 m2 = reduced 'bare corridor lane'; strip: not represented in the reduced model), byp = bypass reach (1.0 m2); ramps excluded (ice, in neither reduced model)
identical_footprint_comparison.compare: cumulative melt volume and mean heat delivery per region, CFD vs reduced topology_lanes() (identical to imported topology.run), at 21 d
identical_footprint_comparison.note: reduced and CFD use the SAME insulation closure (series resistance), so melt agreement tests water delivery to the footprint, not the closure

recovery_classes.definition:
access class relative to the bare-route share f_ref (ordinary access). maintained: never below theta before removal (a removal then cannot 'reconnect' anything); lost-recovered-full: R>=0.5; lost-recovered-partial: 0.05<=R<0.5; lost-not-recovered: R<0.05, where R = mean f over [removal+1 d, end] / f_ref. decline flag: f at end < 0.5 f(removal+1 d).
For runs without removal: maintained / lost. (v1 'sustained reconnection' counted any f>=theta as reconnection and labelled runs that never lost contact as reconnected.)
recovery_classes.f_ref: bare-route share from the bare control run at the same resolution (CFD E01: 0.735-0.738; reduced 0.749)
recovery_classes.applied_to_v1: E03 maintained; E05 maintained(+decline); E06 lost-recovered-partial; E07/E10 lost-not-recovered; E09 maintained(+decline)

bracket_test.pass_criteria: CFD boundary (smallest removal day with f(t_r+1d)<1e-3, linear interpolation over the 5 runs and v1 points 8 d and 12 d) within +-1.0 d of reduced t*=9.50 d; class sequence monotone in removal day

finest_grid_boundary_check.method: fixed-bed post-removal steady flows: bed snapshots of V2M_strip_none (medium) at removal days 8..12 step 0.25, deposit removed, resolved at dx = 0.05, 0.025, 0.0125 (bilinear transfer of the bed); records f_toe at removal+0 per grid; boundary = day where f crosses 1e-3
finest_grid_boundary_check.pass_criteria: boundary shift between dx=0.025 and 0.0125 < 0.5 d; if not, report the finest-grid boundary and flag unresolved. LIMITATION: the bed history is evolved at dx<=0.025 only (bed history spatial sensitivity <1% in melt and 0.25 d in loss time)

acceptance: water/energy residual < 1e-10 per update; failed runs reported, not dropped
